commit_message:
avformat/iamf_parse: add checks to parameter definition durations

Section 3.6.1 of the IAMF spec states "When constant_subblock_duration is equal to 0, the summation of all
subblock_duration in this parameter block SHALL be equal to duration.".

Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>

findings.title: Memory leak of param on failure path in param_parse
findings.message: The newly added validation check for subblock durations at line 570-573 returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA when total_duration != duration, but fails to free the previously allocated `param` object (allocated via av_iamf_param_definition_alloc at line 533). Other error paths in the same function (e.g., the default case in the switch at line 566, the inconsistent parameters check later, and the ENOMEM path) correctly call av_free(param) before returning, but this newly introduced error path was missed. This results in a 48-byte memory leak each time this error path is triggered by a malformed IAMF input file.
findings.suggestion: Add av_free(param) before the return statement on the failure path at line 572, consistent with all other error paths after param allocation in this function.

ground_truth.root_cause: Commit d38fc25519cf12a9212dadcba1258fc176ffbade added a new validation check for subblock durations in param_parse, but the author forgot to include an av_free(param) call on this new error path. The param object had been allocated earlier via av_iamf_param_definition_alloc(), and all other error paths after this allocation correctly free param before returning, but this newly added path was missed.
